reviews.review:
Risk of Rain gives me emotions about heat seeking missiles that I never knew I had. I got blisters on my thumbs from gripping my controller for 2 hours straight with such ferocity, I could have strangled a bear. I made art that would make Jackson Pollock weep. This game made me into a God, and I still had time to go to work and get my shopping done.

Mm-mm. S'good. 11/10 heart shaped missiles locked onto this game.
This is honestly one of the best rogue-like games i've ever played.

[h1]* * * * * MULTIPLAYER WARNING * * * * *[/H1]
[b][u]GAME DOES NOT HAVE STEAM MATCHMAKING. MULTIPLAYER REQUIRES VPN (HAMACHI/EVOLVE/ETC.) OR PORT FORWARDING.[/u][/b]

[h1]2019 UPDATE[/h1]
Does this game work w/ new steam remote play? i.e. maybe u don't need to do the hamachi thing any more? IDK, but it probably might. I can't be arsed to find out for sure.

[h1]OVERVIEW[/h1]
roguelike platform-shooter -- u want to like this game but it's a bit rough around the edges tbh. it's basically "no frills".

but, recommended or not, you should know that my original purpose in writing this review is to let you know that this game isn't as cool as i thought it was going to be, or was hoping it was going to be. :/

I have had mixed feelings about this game and the changing state of this review has reflected that. Originally, "3 out of 5 stars.", but now that I've seen my way to the bigger picture afa how you are supposed to "achieve the impossible", I'll go 3.5. There are still some design/low-budget issues that I find somewhat unforgivable so I'm not going any higher than that.

At first the game is extremely unforgiving. But once you reach the point where you unlock a few of the OP items/mods, it suddenly becomes easy. Depending on how long u want to grind for items in a given session, it can be "too" easy.

Playthrough to playthrough, RNG is definitely a HUGE factor. I guess this is roguelike but it can be frustrating as well as leading to degenerate gameplay where u "reroll" the first level, for example, to get a good map layout.

just fyi, in general, gameplay-wise, for most characters, the game is much more about evasion than stand-and-fight. much!

have to mention also, I think most gamers really can do without the annoying juvenile aspects like insulting messages when you "fail" (or, should I say: "when the game/rng fails you"?), and degenerate achievements where you have to kneecap yourself to achieve the silly grind instead of just allowing you to play the game in a sensible, "play to win" fashion. the style of game design where devs have to turn every product into their personal festering dumpster of bad ideas (the "mcmillan school", i think it's called)? ... hopefully we will move beyond that, soon.

[h1]BARE-BONES MULTIPLAYER[/H1]
The lack of proper MP support is a huge peeve.

I'll assume you're one of the roughly 5-10% of players who can actually be bothered to overcome such barriers to entry as "needs hamachi", and explain some of what you're in for...

First of all: not that many ppl playing and there is no pub matchmaking system in the game at all. U will have to set up games in forums or w/ steam friends.

Be sure to type the correct IP cuz if u try to connect to the wrong one u just have to sit thru a 30-second timeout period while the game acts like it is locked up. no "cancel" button. (no frills. ;P it's a recurring theme.) I presume LAN MP works fine without extra gyrations but u still may have to allow ports through firewall on each machine.

Co-op, u want to play w/ friends who want to win and will cooperate with you to do so. cuz there is almost nothing to enforce "good", "wise", or "fair" play. if there is a way to tell how much $ or health your partner has, I didn't see it.

[h1]GENERAL COMMENTS ABOUT GAMEPLAY/'ROGUELIKES'[/H1]
overall it's fun but early on (before the OP unlocks, like I said), for my particular tastes the abuse:reward ratio is a bit high. in addition to the gameplay itself being very challenging, QoL is rather challenged too. e.g. you tend to spend a lot of time running around empty maps just to (gather any remaining $ in order to) maximize powerups before the next level. nothing u wouldn't do in a typical roguelike or rpg but the running itself is tediously slow. the maps are big and the chars not that fast at the start.

[h1]RE: ZOOM LEVEL[/H1]
another aspect of the design I have always found questionable, that I feel the need to mention... The trailers etc. for the game all seem to be shown in "3x zoom". at this size, the game [i]looks[/i] fun: you can see your character and the action well.

But once you start actually playing the game, you realize that this zoom level does not show you enough of the world itself, as far as what is offscreen and how to navigate your way around nearby screens. i.e. if you stick with such a zoomed-in view, like 3x or 4x, it may take you 20-30 minutes just to explore a single map! (ouch! plus, there are other aspects of the game design (i.e. master timer!) which strongly suggest you are [i]not[/i] supposed to play through the game so slowly!)

To summarize it slightly differently: if you play on one of the "higher" zoom levels (3x or 4x) i.e. zoomed-in "too far", you are going to run into a lot of places in the level-design where it [i]seems[/i] like you should be climbing such-and-such ladder to get where you want to go, but if u were able to see the whole map, u would realize that actually that ladder is a red herring and u want to go a different route entirely. (in some game-review circles, this would aptly be known as "artificial difficulty" or leading to "artificially inflated playtimes". ;P)

So, you will probably try "2x zoom", which lets you see more of the world but your guy is smaller. This is probably the most flexible setting overall and what I used most of the time. (Not a big enough FOV to see everything u want of the world, yet too big of an FOV to see your guy as clearly as you would like. ;P)

"1x" lets you see most of the world, but your guy is so small you can barely see it. But once you know your way around the tactics of the game for each individual character, 1x zoom is basically a hack, because seeing so much of the world at once lets you strategize much more effectively.

and "4x" -- the highest level of zoom -- probably lets you see your guy quite well, and the world quite poorly. I've never used it.

In short, [i]NONE[/i] of these zoom levels seems ideal, which to me means the real issue is w/ map/player/monster/skill/weapon design. i.e. if you want the "default" zoom to be able to show an entire ladder or entire "set" of platforms and ladders etc, on screen at once, then maybe make the maps smaller, or add some sort of other navigational aids: teleporters, signage, etc.

==================

In closing, I found this game a bit of a tough nut to crack but it was something I [i]wanted[/i] to like -- and other ppl seem to like it, as well as the sequel -- so I kept grinding and eventually made my peace with it, more or less.

The only thing I would consider a real showstopper is the MP implementation. Other than that, if you [i]think[/i] you like this game, you probably will, and I recommend it, even if with a bit of a latent grudge. ;P
